findings.claim: The conditional emission excludes netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on both. Generated code for those supported targets therefore has no active attribute, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated; conditional emission is only justified where the attribute is unavailable.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator tests with parse options defining NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK, compiling against netstandard2.0 and net462 reference assemblies respectively, and assert that every generated class has an active ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. On HEAD the guarded attributes are absent. In the same target compilations, compile a source class directly decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute to establish that removing the guard is valid.

findings.claim: An unrelated change formats decimals with StandardFormat('F'). Fixed-point formatting without an explicit precision rounds to the framework's default number of decimal places, so values such as 0.001m can be serialized as "0.00" and 1.234m as "1.23", losing data and changing the stable wire representation. This is outside the code-coverage feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Using base-built and head-built MessagePack assemblies, serialize 0.001m and 1.234m with MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<decimal> under the same default options, compare the MessagePack string payload bytes, and round-trip the HEAD payload. BASE preserves "0.001" and "1.234"; HEAD emits fixed-format rounded strings and round-trips different numeric values.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The implemented reading: decorate every generated formatter, resolver, nested cache and helper class, add no setting, and use preprocessor guards so NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK output contains no attribute.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: The stricter portability reading: 'all generated code' includes netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework, so remove those guards and emit the attribute unconditionally on supported frameworks, still without adding a setting.
